nodes.description: RLYB212, a subcutaneous monoclonal anti-HPA-1a antibody, is in development to prevent maternal HPA-1a alloimmunization, on the model of anti-D prophylaxis in RhD disease. In a Phase 1b proof-of-concept study using an antigen-challenge model of a 30 mL fetal-maternal hemorrhage, it eliminated HPA-1a-positive platelets in a concentration-dependent manner and was well tolerated. It is investigational and not licensed; there is at present no treatment that prevents HPA alloimmunization or FNAIT.

nodes.description: A distinct subtype of anti-HPA-1a binds endothelial alphaV-beta3 rather than platelet alphaIIb-beta3. This anti-alphaV-beta3 subtype induces endothelial apoptosis through caspase-3/7 activation and reactive oxygen species, and interferes with endothelial adhesion to vitronectin and with tube formation. It is found in mothers whose pregnancies had intracranial hemorrhage and not in those whose pregnancies did not.

A newborn with severe thrombocytopenia is transfused to prevent or treat bleeding. nodes.description: The HPA-1 system is defined by a single Leu33Pro substitution on the PSI domain of the integrin beta-3 chain (platelet glycoprotein IIIa, ITGB3); the Leu33 form is HPA-1a. A fetus that inherits HPA-1a from the father carries the antigen on its platelet alphaIIb-beta3 and on endothelial alphaV-beta3. When the pregnant person is HPA-1b/1b, that antigen is foreign and can prime an alloimmune response. The beta-3 chain's own molecular function is unchanged by which HPA-1 allele it carries: this is a common blood-group polymorphism, not a pathogenic lesion in the affected individual, and the fibrinogen-binding function named here identifies the receptor the epitope sits on rather than asserting any loss of it.

nodes.description: Anti-HPA-1a IgG1 in these pregnancies carries markedly less core fucose at the Fc glycan than total serum IgG1 does. Afucosylated IgG1 binds FcgammaRIIIa and FcgammaRIIIb with higher affinity, and the degree of fucosylation correlates positively with the neonatal platelet count and negatively with clinical severity. This is a quantitative property of the antibody rather than of its specificity, and it is part of why antibody level alone predicts bleeding poorly.

nodes.description: Beyond destroying circulating platelets, maternal anti-HPA-1a sera reduce megakaryocyte numbers in culture by inducing apoptosis and death of early megakaryocytes and megakaryocyte progenitors, while the surviving cells mature normally. Impaired production therefore contributes to the low neonatal platelet count alongside accelerated clearance, and the degree of suppression correlates with the platelet count at birth.

nodes.description: Maternal anti-HPA-1a IgG crosses the placenta into the fetal circulation, transported across syncytiotrophoblast by the neonatal Fc receptor. This transfer is the step that converts a maternal immune response into fetal disease, and it is why the fetus is affected without carrying any lesion of its own beyond the antigen.
